rows.grounds: first member of compound with tejaḥ
second member of compound ravi-tejaḥ, having sun-like splendor
planet Venus, also preceptor of demons

items.question: Which celestial and preceptorial figures are identified as foremost in their respective domains?
premises: The moon-lord possesses sun-like splendor and is best.
Venus is identified as the lord of poets.
items.inference: The moon-lord and Venus are presented as supreme exemplars in their spheres.
items.plain_english: The lord of stars, radiant like the sun, is the best; Venus is the lord of poets.

items.question: Which elemental and divine figures are declared foremost among purifiers, Rudras, and teachers?
premises: Wind and pure fire are declared the best.
Shankara is the king of Rudras and the teacher.
items.inference: Elemental forces and Shiva are identified as supreme in purity, rulership, and guidance.
items.plain_english: Wind and pure fire are the best; Shankara is the king of the Rudras and the teacher.

items.question: Which primordial sound, goddess, power, and sage are ranked as foremost in their categories?
premises: The beginning of letters is foremost and Gauri is the foremost woman.
Shri is the foremost power and Narada is included among the foremost.
items.inference: Primordial sound, Gauri, Shri, and Narada are presented as supreme in their respective domains.
uncertainties: varṇādir may refer to the syllable 'a' or to color/beginning; taken as beginning of letters
items.plain_english: The first of letters is foremost, Gauri is the foremost woman, Shri is the foremost power, and Narada is foremost.

rows.grounds: compound yādasām-patiḥ, lord of aquatic beings

items.question: Which deities are identified as supreme among winds and aquatic beings?
premises: Pavana is identified as the lord of winds.
Varuna is identified as the lord of aquatic beings.
items.inference: Pavana and Varuna hold supreme lordship over wind and water creatures respectively.
items.plain_english: Pavana is the lord of the winds, and Varuna is the lord of aquatic creatures.

rows.grounds: compound sudarśana-astra-agryaḥ, foremost among weapons is Sudarshana
compound vajra-praharaṇa-uttamam, thunderbolt as best striking weapon

items.question: Which substances and weapons are declared foremost in nourishment and martial power?
premises: Food is presented as foremost in its category.
Sudarshana is the foremost weapon and the thunderbolt is the best striking weapon.
items.inference: Food, Sudarshana, and the thunderbolt are identified as supreme in their respective domains.
items.plain_english: Food is foremost; the Sudarshana is the foremost weapon, and the thunderbolt is the best striking weapon.

rows.grounds: compound eka-patnī-īśaḥ, lord devoted to one wife
compound aśeṣa-vṛkṣa-rāj, king of all trees

items.question: Which woman, husband, and tree are exalted as supreme exemplars of fidelity and kingship?
premises: Arundhati is foremost and the lord devoted to one wife is supreme.
The sacred fig tree is indeed the king of all trees.
items.inference: Arundhati, the one-wife lord, and the sacred fig tree are presented as supreme exemplars.
uncertainties: ekapatnīśo may refer to Rama as the ideal husband devoted to one wife
items.plain_english: Arundhati is foremost, the lord devoted to one wife is supreme, and indeed the sacred fig tree is the king of all trees.

rows.grounds: compound sāma-agryaḥ, foremost among Sama chants

items.question: Which mountain, path, chant, and time are declared the best in their respective classes?
premises: Meru is the lord of mountains.
The path, the foremost Sama chant, and the best time are identified as supreme.
items.inference: Meru, the path, the foremost Sama, and the best time are presented as preeminent.
uncertainties: mārgo may refer to a specific spiritual path or path in general
items.plain_english: Meru is the lord of mountains, the path is foremost, the Sama is the foremost chant, and it is the best of times.

items.question: Which bird, priest, season, and tree are identified as foremost in their domains?
premises: Tarkshya is the king of birds.
The foremost priest, spring, and the wish-fulfilling tree are supreme in their classes.
items.inference: Garuda, the foremost priest, spring, and the wish-fulfilling tree are presented as preeminent.
uncertainties: ṛtvagryo may refer to a specific priestly role or the best officiating priest
items.plain_english: Tarkshya is the king of birds, the foremost priest, spring is the foremost season, and the wish-fulfilling tree is foremost.

rows.grounds: compound mātā-ahitatamaḥ, mother as most beneficial; reading follows given form

items.question: Which jewel, teacher, and parental figures are declared the most excellent and beneficial?
premises: The wish-fulfilling jewel and the best teacher are foremost.
The mother is most beneficial and the father is foremost.
items.inference: The wish-fulfilling jewel, the best teacher, mother, and father are presented as supreme.
uncertainties: mātāhitatamaḥ is read as mother most beneficial; compound formation is unusual
items.plain_english: The wish-fulfilling jewel is foremost, the best teacher is foremost, the mother is most beneficial, and the father is foremost.

rows.grounds: possibly amaḥ or part of salutation; reading uncertain

items.question: Which social, inner, and devotional elements are affirmed as foremost and worthy of obeisance?
premises: The lord of letters and the brahmin are foremost.
The foremost inner organ is affirmed with obeisance.
items.inference: Supreme status is assigned to the lord of letters, the brahmin, the inner organ, and obeisance is offered.
uncertainties: amo namaḥ reading is uncertain; may be a salutation formula or textual corruption
items.plain_english: The lord of letters, the brahmin, and the foremost inner organ are supreme; obeisance, obeisance.

rows.grounds: compound sarva-aparādha-śamanam, that which pacifies all offenses
compound parama-bhakti-vivardhanam, that which increases supreme devotion

items.question: What spiritual effects of pacifying offenses and increasing devotion are attributed to the subject?
premises: The subject pacifies all offenses.
The subject increases supreme devotion.
items.inference: The subject is characterized as removing faults and fostering supreme devotion.
items.plain_english: It pacifies all offenses and increases supreme devotion.

rows.grounds: compound viṣṇu-loka-eka-sopānam, the sole stairway to Vishnu's world
compound sarva-duḥkha-vināśanam, that which destroys all sorrows

items.question: What salvific and liberating powers are ascribed to the subject regarding Vishnu's world and sorrow?
premises: The subject is the sole stairway to Vishnu's world.
The subject destroys all sorrows.
items.inference: The subject grants access to Vishnu's realm and removes all suffering.
items.plain_english: It is the sole stairway to the world of Vishnu and the destroyer of all sorrows.

rows.grounds: compound kāma-krodha-ādi-niḥśeṣam, completely removing desire, anger, etc.
compound an-amala-viśodhanam, purifying of faults and impurities

items.question: What purifying effects on passions and impurities are attributed to the subject?
premises: The subject completely removes desire, anger, and similar passions.
The subject purifies faults and impurities.
items.inference: The subject eradicates inner passions and cleanses all impurities.
items.plain_english: It completely removes desire, anger, and the rest, and purifies all faults and impurities.

rows.grounds: compound sarva-abhīṣṭa-phala-pradam, giving all desired fruits

items.question: What universal benefit and speed of fulfillment are promised to all living beings?
premises: The subject benefits all living beings.
The subject quickly grants all desired fruits.
items.inference: The subject swiftly fulfills the desires of all creatures.
items.plain_english: It quickly grants all desired fruits to all living beings.

items.question: What relief from severe suffering and poverty is attributed to the subject?
premises: The subject pacifies terrible sorrow.
The subject destroys intense poverty.
items.inference: The subject alleviates extreme suffering and removes severe poverty.
items.plain_english: It pacifies terrible sorrow and destroys intense poverty.

rows.grounds: compound sarva-kāla-dam, giving benefits at all times

items.question: What comprehensive powers, accomplishments, and temporal benefits are bestowed by the subject?
premises: The subject grants all sovereignty and all accomplishments.
The subject gives benefits at all times.
items.inference: The subject bestows complete power, success, and enduring benefits.
uncertainties: sarvakāladam may mean granting all time or effective at all times
items.plain_english: It grants all sovereignty, all accomplishments, and benefits at all times.

rows.grounds: compound aprajñā-jāḍya-śamanam, pacifying lack of wisdom and dullness

items.question: What intellectual transformation from dullness to knowledge is effected by the subject?
premises: The subject pacifies ignorance and dullness.
The subject promotes all knowledge.
items.inference: The subject removes mental dullness and initiates the acquisition of all knowledge.
items.plain_english: It pacifies ignorance and dullness and promotes all knowledge.

rows.grounds: compound sarva-śreṣṭha-phala-pradam, giving all the best fruits

items.question: What immediate boons for progeny and supreme rewards are granted by the subject?
premises: The subject quickly grants sons to barren women.
The subject gives all the best fruits.
items.inference: The subject provides progeny and the highest rewards swiftly.
items.plain_english: It quickly grants sons to barren women and gives all the best fruits.

items.question: What auspicious, meritorious, and life-enhancing results arise from hearing, reciting, and repeating the subject?
premises: The subject is auspicious, meritorious, and life-promoting.
These results arise from hearing, reciting, and repetition.
items.inference: Hearing, reciting, and repeating the subject yield auspiciousness, merit, and long life.
items.plain_english: It is auspicious, meritorious, and life-promoting through hearing, recitation, and repetition.

items.question: What traditional textual practices of reciting and teaching are compared to engaging with this subject?
premises: Puranas, scriptures, and Smritis are recited.
They are likewise caused to be recited.
items.inference: Engagement with this subject is comparable to reciting and teaching traditional sacred texts.
items.plain_english: Puranas, scriptures, and Smritis have been recited and likewise taught to others.

rows.grounds: kim uta, how much more, with sandhi marking

items.question: What certainty and speed of complete success are promised to all practitioners?
premises: Success always comes quickly for all.
How much more so is complete success assured.
items.inference: All practitioners attain success swiftly, and complete fulfillment is even more certain.
items.plain_english: It always succeeds quickly for everyone; how much more so does it succeed entirely.

rows.grounds: compound sva-artha-eka-siddhaye, for attainment of one's own sole purpose

items.question: What injunctions of secrecy and recitation are given for attaining one's own purpose?
premises: This teaching must be kept secret by you.
This teaching must be recited for the attainment of one's own purpose.
items.inference: The teaching is to be guarded and recited to achieve one's intended goal.
items.plain_english: O auspicious one, this must be kept secret by you and recited for the attainment of your own purpose.

rows.grounds: compound bhakti-śraddhā-vihīnāya, to one devoid of devotion and faith
compound viṣṇu-sāmānya-darśine, to one who sees Vishnu as ordinary

items.question: To which kinds of unqualified recipients must this teaching not be disclosed?
premises: The teaching must not be given to one devoid of devotion and faith.
The teaching must not be given to one who regards Vishnu as ordinary.
items.inference: Disclosure is prohibited to those lacking devotion and proper regard for Vishnu.
items.plain_english: It must not be given to one devoid of devotion and faith, or to one who sees Vishnu as ordinary.

rows.grounds: compound alpa-medhasaḥ, those of little intelligence

items.question: Why are the dull-minded unable to receive this teaching without divine grace?
premises: Without my grace, the dull-minded cannot receive this teaching.
Divine grace is required for grasping this teaching.
items.inference: Reception of the teaching depends on grace, which the dull-minded lack without it.
items.plain_english: Without my grace, those of little intelligence will not grasp this.
